note: Both cohorts (Benkirane et al. de novo cases and Torella et al. p.Glu415Lys families) report spastic ataxia with dysarthria, providing a concrete basis to compare phenotypic severity and onset across inheritance modes.

evidence.text: Benkirane et al. report 12 patients presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia harbouring TUBA4A missense variants, including five confirmed de novo cases alongside inherited cases, demonstrating variable age of onset.

source.title: De novo and inherited monoallelic variants in TUBA4A cause ataxia and spasticity
source.quote: Taken together, we report 12 patients presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia and harbouring a predicted pathogenic TUBA4A missense mutation, including five confirmed de novo cases and a mutation previously reported in a large family presenting with spastic ataxia.

evidence.text: Torella et al. characterized two families carrying the familial inherited p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A presenting with autosomal dominant spastic ataxia.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: In the present study, we report two families, one with 11 affected individuals and the other with a single patient, carrying a novel, likely pathogenic, variant (p. Glu415Lys) in the TUBA4A gene (NM_006000).
